items.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001
items.q: Then a slightly later group became very involved with Bunk Johnson and George Lewis. So where I stood was on the King Oliver, Louis Armstrong, Kid Ory line.

ctx.x: Yes we do. I was going to run a few names by you and just maybe make a comment on them. Actually King Oliver was going to be a name.

Again you see at the time I came up or got interested, there was a terrific focus, I mean people like Humphrey Lyttelton were enamored of the work particularly of the King Oliver Creole Jazz Band. And then of course the Louis Armstrong Hot Five. Sandy © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

Brown and Al Fairweather were, you know, bowled over by that group of original innovators. Then a slightly later group became very involved with Bunk Johnson and George Lewis. So where I stood was on the King Oliver, Louis Armstrong, Kid Ory line. And I think I can remember buying my first 78 of the King Oliver Band, you know, “Canal Street Blues,” I mean we knew this was the real thing. And of course the young Louis was in there so that was powerful. To give you a little insight, not to ask, but I remember…
